content.content: {"result":"{\"mimeType\": \"text/markdown\", \"text\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\\n\\nWhat goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.\\n\\nOne Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.\\nFixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.\\nGone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.\\nCovered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.\\nBroken: anything else. File it as Bugs.\\n\\nWhat counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.\\n\\nNew tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.\\n\\nUI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.\\n\\nSheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.\\n\", \"id\": \"f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52\", \"name\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\"}"}

{"mimeType": "text/markdown", "text": "DD bug carry-over notes

What goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.

One Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.
Fixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.
Gone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.
Covered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.
Broken: anything else. File it as Bugs.

What counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.

New tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.

UI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.

Sheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.
", "id": "f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52", "name": "DD bug carry-over notes"}

Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes\nWhen the Canvas is set to *Screen Space \u2013 Camera* (or World Space):\n\u2022 UI is rendered *by a Camera*\n\u2022 It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*\n\u2022 Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera\u2019s render path\n\u2022 On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:\nNot render at all, or\nRender incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)\nThis is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.\n\n2. Screen Space \u2013 Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency\nWhen switching to *Screen Space \u2013 Overlay*:\n\u2022 UI is rendered *after the scene*\n\u2022 It bypasses:\nCameras\nLighting\nShadows\nPost-processing\nSo the bottom bar becomes visible again.\nHowever, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.\n If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.\nIn other words:\n> Overlay mode didn\u2019t break character visuals \u2014 it *revealed an existing dependency*.\n3. Why this happens only on some Android devices\nDifferent Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:\n\u2022 They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently\n\u2022 URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently\n\u2022 Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors\nThis is why:\n\u2022 The issue does not reproduce on all devices\n\u2022 It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes\nKey Takeaway\nThe core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:\n> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*\nScreen Space \u2013 Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.", "channel": 1766416589.444619 thr= 1766415326.501939 Brian Foster   | Why This Issue Is Happening (Root Cause) / This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*. / 1. Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes / When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space): / • UI is rendered *by a Camera* / • It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene* / • Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera’s render path / • On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to: / Not render at all, or / Render incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues) / This is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*. /  / 2. Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency / When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*: / • UI is rendered *after the scene* / • It bypasses: / Cameras / Lighting / Shadows / Post-processing / So the bottom bar becomes visible again. / However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene. /  If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately. / In other words: / > Overlay mode didn’t break character visuals — it *revealed an existing dependency*. / 3. Why this happens only on some Android devices / Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and: / • They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently / • URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently / • Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors / This is why: / • The issue does not reproduce on all devices / • It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes / Key Takeaway / The core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that: / > *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.* / Screen Space – Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.

1766416589.444619 thr= 1766415326.501939 Brian Foster   | Why This Issue Is Happening (Root Cause) / This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*. / 1. Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes / When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space): / • UI is rendered *by a Camera* / • It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene* / • Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera’s render path / • On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to: / Not render at all, or / Render incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues) / This is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*. /  / 2. Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency / When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*: / • UI is rendered *after the scene* / • It bypasses: / Cameras / Lighting / Shadows / Post-processing / So the bottom bar becomes visible again. / However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene. /  If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately. / In other words: / > Overlay mode didn’t break character visuals — it *revealed an existing dependency*. / 3. Why this happens only on some Android devices / Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and: / • They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently / • URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently / • Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors / This is why: / • The issue does not reproduce on all devices / • It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes / Key Takeaway / The core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that: / > *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.* / Screen Space – Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.

• The main purpose of showing users their inventory is to make them aware of tokens they might have accumulated without realizing it. However, when we add the inventory to the profile section, I think users have to go through too many steps to access it. As a result, users who are not curious may not frequently check their inventory, leading them to remain unaware of the tokens they've accumulated.
• Additionally, having such an inventory could allow users to make more informed decisions when selecting packages from the store in the future.
Therefore, instead of showing users their inventory directly, I would like to propose the following suggestion:
• We can create a systematic and customizable panel. 
• This panel should be triggered according to the user's inventory and remind them of the tokens they have collected (of course it should be triggered at a certain time period, e.g. once a week).
• For example, a message like “You have collected XX tokens, let's spend them!” could appear with an illustration and direct users to the relevant section with a button on the panel.
• If the user is not interested, they can close the panel and continue playing.

4. Changing to multi breaks all references to the sprite. The tool fixes up all references across the whole project.
5. Then as a final step we can apply special compression and settings per platform.

Dataset
• *18 lost attempts* (App versions: *1.0.56 = 15*, *1.0.57 = 3*)
• All rows have the key gameplay fields populated.
Do losers buy pieces?
Yes, always.
*18/18 (100%)* bought pieces.
• Pieces bought distribution: *median 7*, p25 *5.25*, p75 *9*, range *2–12*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t buying” is not the issue.

Do losers sell pieces?
Rarely (for actual tiles).
• *Tiles Sold Int > 0:* *6/18 (33%)*
Tiles sold: median *0*, p75 *1*, max *9*.
• *Trash Sold Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
Trash sold: median *8*, range *2–18*.
Takeaway: if “selling tiles” is a core mechanic, adoption is low. Trash selling looks universal, so either it is easy/automatic, or it is the only “sell” behavior players understand.

Do losers remove obstacles?
Yes, always.
*Obstacles Removed Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
• Obstacles removed: *median 4*, p75 *6*, range *1–7*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t removing obstacles” is not supported by this dataset.

Do losers build combos?
You still do not log combos directly, but *Highest Dps Int* is your best proxy.
• Highest DPS: *median 508.5*, p75 *621*, max *1189*.
Takeaway: many losing runs ramp to substantial DPS, especially in late deaths, so a large part of the problem is not “no combos,” it is “combos not enough to survive the late curve” or “spend not converting to survivability.”

What does Silver Balance Int tell us?
Everyone dies with silver left.
• *Silver Balance Int*: median *84*, p75 *108*, max *160*, min *38*.
Takeaway: players are not ending at “0 resources.” They are dying with spendable currency still in hand, which usually points to one of:
1. spend options are not impactful enough to change outcomes,
2. shop decisions are unclear (players buy the wrong things),
3. shop timing/UX friction (they do not spend at the right moment).
How behavior changes by where they die
Segmented by *Highest Wave Reached Int*:
Early deaths (<= 6), N=4
Pieces bought median *4.5*
Obstacles removed median *2*
DPS median *178*
Silver median *67*
• Tiles sold any *25%*
Interpretation: these are “didn’t ramp” runs, likely skill/understanding + early variance.
Mid deaths (7–9), N=4
Pieces bought median *6*
Obstacles removed median *4.5*
DPS median *376.5*
Silver median *71*
• Tiles sold any *50%* (highest of the three groups)
Interpretation: midgame wall starts showing, some players try selling as a recovery move.
Late deaths (>= 10), N=10
Pieces bought median *9*
Obstacles removed median *5.5*
DPS median *611*
Silver median *107*
• Tiles sold any *30%*
Interpretation: late losers are actively playing the systems (buying, clearing, ramping DPS) and still die, often with meaningful silver left. That is tuning plus spend-impact, not “they didn’t engage.”

What you should change (based on this)
If you want win rate to move hard, focus on two things.
1) Make spending convert into survival
You have clear evidence of “dies with silver left,” especially in late runs.
Add *recommended purchase* (one button) when HP is low or wave >= 10 and silver >= X.
• Add *auto-open shop* at wave checkpoints (ex: after wave 6 and wave 10) with 1–2 highlighted options.
• Buff the best defensive/sustain option so it reliably prevents late deaths (shield, lifesteal, regen spike, damage reduction).
2) Decide whether tile-selling is supposed to matter
Because Tiles Sold is only *33%*:
• If selling is intended core: force it in FTUE once, and add a contextual prompt when the board is tight (“sell lowest value tile” preselected).
• If selling is optional: stop assuming it is the reason for losses, and tune the level assuming most players will not sell tiles.
One logging gap to close
To prove your theory cleanly, you need:
• *Silver spent total* and *purchase types* (offense vs defense vs utility), plus *time since last purchase*.
Right now you only know they _bought some pieces_ and _had silver left_. You cannot tell whether they failed because they did not spend, or because they spent on weak/wrong things.

{"result":"{\"id\": \"page_qa_runbook\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"QA Regression Runbook\", \"body\": \"

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Last owned by QA (Arthur Blake, who took it over from Vincent Parker when Vincent Parker left in Nov 2025; Arthur Blake stayed through the February 2026 wind-down); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (listed as \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" until the July 2025 rename) and Combo Fighter. Budget a few hours per title - the first five chapters alone run over an hour; if something fails, file the bug and block the release, don't hand-wave it.

Test the UPDATE path, not just a fresh install. The June 2025 progression losses were on Domino Delights, and nobody ever reproduced them - the leading hypothesis was the update path, which is why we test it. Every candidate must be installed over the last two shipped versions and checked for save/progression loss before we ship. If we only test fresh installs we will miss this entire class of bug again.

Recurring bug classes to always check

These four have all bitten us in production. Treat them as non-negotiable checks on every pass, on real devices, not just the emulator.

  • Font / asset download stall on splash. In May 2025 Domino Delights froze at roughly 22% on the splash screen while pulling remote fonts and assets (ENG-2346, build 0.2.197). Watch the loading bar all the way to gameplay; test on a throttled/slow connection and with the app cache cleared.
  • Lives & scheduler regeneration. Confirm lives tick back up on the timer, refill correctly after device clock changes, and that offline time is credited without over-granting.
  • Quest population & reset. New quests populate on a fresh session, complete correctly, and roll over at the daily/weekly reset without duplicating or leaving empty slots.
  • Save / progression integrity. Level, coins and unlocks survive an update, a force-quit and a re-launch. This is the one the June 2025 wipe belongs to.

Regression matrix

Run each row on at least one iOS and one Android device. Both update rows are mandatory - N-1 and N-2 are the last two shipped store versions.

AreaFresh installUpdate from N-1Update from N-2Notes
Splash / asset loadPassPassPassWatch for the ~22% stall (May 2025 Domino Delights)
Save / progressionPassPassPassJune 2025 wipe never reproduced in-house; update path is the leading hypothesis
Lives & schedulerPassPassPassTest with device clock changes
Quests populate / resetPassPassPassCheck daily + weekly rollover
Purchase / restorePassPassPassSandbox account. NOTE: entitlements do not restore on reinstall and receipts are not validated server-side - see the per-title IAP row below. Check the purchase grants client-side, not that it restores.

If a check fails

  • File the bug with device, OS version, source build and repro steps, and link it here.
  • A failure in any UPDATE column blocks the release - fresh-install-only regressions do not pass the gate.

This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*.
1. Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes
When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space):
• UI is rendered *by a Camera*
• It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*
• Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera’s render path
• On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:
Not render at all, or
Render incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)
This is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.

2. Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency
When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*:
• UI is rendered *after the scene*
• It bypasses:
Cameras
Lighting
Shadows
Post-processing
So the bottom bar becomes visible again.
However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.
 If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.
In other words:
> Overlay mode didn’t break character visuals — it *revealed an existing dependency*.
3. Why this happens only on some Android devices
Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:
• They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently
• URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently
• Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors
This is why:
• The issue does not reproduce on all devices
• It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes
Key Takeaway
The core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:
> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*

* Implement tickets as the new entry currency: 1 ticket or 1 000 coins or timed infinite ticket to play.
* Add 3 play button states (coins, ticket count, timed infinite).
* Remove lives from HUD, minigames, rewards, shop, season pass, Nate, quests, FTUE, and out-of-lives flow.
* Introduce tickets in daily/weekly chests and the new FTUE quest.

2. **Make the game harder**

* Nerf [PERSON_NAME_3999]’s Favor so it gives fewer tiles and coins.

3. **Rebalance rewards**

* Update event and LiveOps reward tables to reduce free boosters, remove infinite lives, and add some ticket or gem rewards where specified.

4. **Tighten coin and upgrade economy**

* Switch character upgrades from coins to gems using the new gem cost table.
* Keep coins focused on level entry.

5. **Dynamic difficulty**

* Update dynamic difficulty to use the new nerfed assistance rules from the design doc.

6. **Optional difficulty increase**

"message", "text": "```private void UnlockHarmonyButton(TutorialAction action)
{
    var lockUI = action as TutorialActionUnLockUI;

    LockedButtons.Remove(lockUI.ObjectId);
    DominoPlayerPrefs.SaveLockedButtons(LockedButtons);
    DominoPlayerPrefs.SetMinigameUnlocked(lockUI.ObjectId);

    var harmonyObject = FindHarmonyObjectByName(lockUI.ObjectId, 0);

    if (harmonyObject == null)
    {
        // Check if memory game
        if (lockUI.ObjectId.Equals(DominoConstants.MemoryGameKey))
        {
            MiniGamesManager manager = FindObjectOfType<MiniGamesManager>();
            if (manager != null)
            {
                manager.UnlockMemoryGame();
            }
        }
        return;
    }

    var harmonyButton = harmonyObject as HarmonyButton;
    if (harmonyButton == null)
    {
        HL.LogError(HC.Tutorial, $"Object |{lockUI.ObjectId}| does not have HarmonyButton component to lock");
        return;
    }

    UnlockButton(harmonyButton);
}

private void UnlockButton(HarmonyButton harmonyButton)
{
    harmonyButton.interactable = true;

    // Remove lock icon
    var panelLock = harmonyButton.GameObject.transform.Find("LockIcon");
    if (panelLock != null)
    {
        Destroy(panelLock.gameObject);
    }

    // Remove input block
    var inputBlock = harmonyButton.GameObject.transform.Find("TooltipLocked");
    if (inputBlock != null)
    {
        Destroy(inputBlock.gameObject);
    }

    // Remove TooltipButton
    var tooltipButton = harmonyButton.GameObject.transform.Find("TooltipButton");
    if (tooltipButton != null)
    {

Display cutout handling

Full-screen mode at runtime

Read Screen.safeArea once in Start()

Apply padding once

Never re-apply after resolution/orientation/system-UI changes

Is anchored to bottom

Match slider ≠ 0.5

OnePlus gesture bar:

Takes space at bottom

Sometimes reported as top inset

Causes Unity to offset UI upward

Screen.fullScreen = true;

cd /app/mpdm; python3 - <<'EOF' > all.txt
import json,glob
for f in sorted(glob.glob('p*.txt')):
    d=json.loads(json.load(open(f))['result'])
    for m in d['messages']:
        if not m['text'].strip(): continue
        print(m['ts'], m.get('time','')[:16], (m.get('user_profile') or {}).get('name','?'), 'thr='+m.get('thread_ts','-'), '|', m['text'].replace('\n',' / '))
EOF
wc -l all.txt; grep -inE "apple|sign.?in|train|snow|navigation|nav bar|leave team|quit|backend error|lives|life|charact|shop icon|round icon|river ?tile|memory|flicker|music|mega|acid|nate|treasure|axe|bottom bar|tile dozer|plinko|lucky|win.?and.?collect|collect|season pass|daily gift|disabled|switch|turn(ed)? off|rule|linear|ticket.*done|close (the|this|it)|chapter 4|addressable|cache|splash|tavern|offer|avatar|purple|banner|prelevel|retry|outline|continue|activate|price|streak|teams|saga|cloud|music" all.txt | cut -c1-400 | head -300

Instead of\\n1 consecutive win - 1 extra tile at start\\n2 consecutive wins - 2 extra tiles at start\\n3 consecutive wins - 2 extra tiles and 1 wild tile at hand at start\\n\\nwe will have\\n\\n1 consecutive win - 100 coins at start (effectively ~10% discount on level cost, depending on what type of level difficulty the level has (i.e. normal, hard, epic))\\n2 consecutive wins - 1 extra tile at start\\n3 consecutive wins - 2 extra tiles at start\\n\\nWe also decreased the amount of early assistance, boosting chance of players to pull a relevant card from the deck\\n\\nIn addition, live ops now drops less pre-level and in-level boosters as rewards but give more tickets and stars to help managing the new coin balancing of the game and making characters upgrades a bit easier from star economy perspective.\\n\\nThe final big change in terms of economy is character upgrades now use gems instead of coins, saving players from the confusion of where to spend their coins on. content.text:
Everything Arthur asked for is done ahead of Sunday's bug review, and I've replied in his DM thread with the three numbers: **8 still broken, 69 new tickets, 25 of 28 UI children Done.** Every call was judged against Android 0.3.310, the build players have. It came off the economy line, and I confirmed in GitHub that the branch it was built from contains the economy-line commits.

**What went over (70 records)**
- 63 lines from Vincent's "Bugs on Android 2231" canvas. Six comments whose canvas lines had been deleted were skipped, as the notes say.
- 7 bug posts from #god-bugs made after the last canvas line. Follow-ups were folded into their bugs. Arthur's no-ads question to Leonard and Robert's QA-doc post were left out, as were Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel.

**Linear tickets**
- 69 new tickets, ENG-2438 to ENG-2506. Each is on the Engineering team with the Bug label, sits under ENG-2401, has no assignee or description, and starts with the "[2231]" prefix Arthur later asked for on ENG-2401.
- 59 are Done (fixed), 3 are Canceled (gone) and 7 are in Bugs (broken).
- The 3 Canceled are canvas lines about lives. Lives were replaced by tickets on the economy line, so 0.3.310 has none.
- One line, the Android manual sign-in getting stuck, wasn't filed. Vincent had already tied it to open ENG-2363, so I added the canvas wording there as a note.
- The 7 still broken:
  - the Apple sign-in/sync line
  - the backend errors after losing a level
  - the train level backgrounds
  - the nav bar vanishing after quitting a team
  - the round shop icons in River Tile and Memory Tile. This line was ticked, but Brian said on Dec 1 the icons were back and not to trust the tick.
  - the megatile missing a face
  - the Tile Dozer background. Marcus's fix is PR #1913, which was never merged.

**UI Changes tree**
- 16 open children moved to Done; the 9 already Done stayed Done. The masters weren't touched.
- Three stay open: Collect & Win (ENG-2424) is switched off in 0.3.310, Season Pass (ENG-2428) still uses the old reward track frames per Oliver, and Daily Gift (ENG-2437) never got its last pass per Brian.
- All 28 children have a comment saying where they landed and naming 0.3.310 as the current public build. That follows Brian's closing rule, which I found as a comment on the "UI optimization pass" Trello card.

**Sheet**
"DD bug carry-over (Android 2231 canvas + #god-bugs)" is in your DD bug carry-over folder with columns Bug, Outcome, Ticket and Why. It's shared read-only with the review invitees: Arthur, Robert and Oliver.

**Decisions to check**
- **Titles:** they keep the original text, including ":warning:" and the redacted name placeholders. Slack user tags are written as "@Name".
- **Two Done calls rest on commits whose names don't spell out the bug:**
  - Robert's music post: Owen's "Updated URLAudioPlayer to fully download clip if needed" (Dec 5).
  - Nate's delayed acid animation: "Nathan Animation Fix" (Dec 5).

  If Arthur reads "a commit named for the bug" strictly, these two flip to broken, giving 10 still broken.
